extracted.intended_audience: U.S. practitioners/attorneys representing trademark applicants before the USPTO (trademark practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and disciplinary expectations for attorneys practicing trademark law before the USPTO, including duties under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, the U.S. Counsel Rule (37 C.F.R. §2.11), and related TMEP obligations. Covers what constitutes misconduct, corrective actions, mitigating factors, and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent representation (37 C.F.R. §11.101)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must know and understand the USPTO trademark rules; failing to ensure knowledge of the rules may result in violations. The Order emphasizes that competency includes understanding trademark rules (e.g., specimen standards, Section 1(a) vs 1(b)) and knowing who the client is. Cited as basis for discipline where respondent 'did not adequately understand the ethics and trademark rules' and her reviews were sometimes inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. §11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires taking reasonable steps to ensure clients' trademark filings comply with USPTO trademark rules; failure (e.g., inadequate review of filings) supports discipline. The respondent's failure to ensure filings were filed in accordance with rules was cited as a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications with client (37 C.F.R. §11.104(a) and (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must communicate with clients; provide information so clients can make informed decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes informing clients about actual or potential adverse consequences of not complying with USPTO trademark rules (e.g., what constitutes a proper specimen, differences between Section 1(a) and Section 1(b) applications). The respondent failed to take reasonable steps to ensure KA provided applicants with information Respondent provided regarding important legal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to integrity of the trademark registration system (37 C.F.R. §11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must avoid conduct prejudicial to the integrity of the U.S. trademark registration system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically includes failing to take reasonable steps to ensure specimens were reviewed diligently and were not mock-ups but bona fide examples of the mark as used in commerce. Such failures can undermine the integrity and accuracy of the register and support discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Counsel Rule / Requirement of U.S. licensed attorney for foreign-domiciled applicants (37 C.F.R. §2.11; 84 FR 31498-01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants, registrants, or parties to a trademark proceeding whose domicile is not located within the U.S. or its territories must be represented by an attorney who is an active member in good standing of the bar of the highest court of a state in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to increase compliance with U.S. trademark law, improve accuracy of submissions, and safeguard register integrity. The Order explains why the rule was adopted (to reduce unauthorized practice by foreign parties, reduce mock-up/digitally altered specimens, and improve accuracy). Practitioners are expected to be reasonably well informed of the U.S. Counsel Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to know the identity of the client
rubrics_metrics.description: A USPTO practitioner has an ethical obligation to know who the client is (citing 37 C.F.R. §11.101 and §11.804(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working with a foreign intermediary the client is the trademark applicant; receiving instructions through a foreign agent does not change that. Practitioners must take reasonable steps to avoid foreseeable prejudice to clients' rights and to know the identities of their clients (cites Responsibilities of Practitioners and case law).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide review of specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners representing trademark applicants are expected to undertake a bona fide review of specimens submitted in support of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review should detect mock-ups or digitally altered specimens and ensure specimen shows actual use in commerce. Failure to do so undermines the accuracy and integrity of the register and supports discipline (the Order cites examples of mock-ups and altered specimens filed by foreign applicants/intermediaries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and comply with signature and filing requirements (TMEP, 37 C.F.R. §2.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must know USPTO signature requirements and applicable TMEP provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sanction requires the respondent to review thoroughly all TMEP provisions (including signature requirements), 37 C.F.R. §2.11, and commentary on Requirement of U.S. Licensed Attorney. Compliance with signature/filing rules is necessary to avoid improper filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clients with required information about filing type and specimen requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must ensure clients receive information regarding important legal issues such as what constitutes a proper specimen and differences between Section 1(a) and Section 1(b) applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent failed to take reasonable steps to ensure KA provided applicants with information Respondent provided to KA about these issues. Proper client communication is part of competent representation and informed decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take corrective action for potential harm caused by improper representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner has responsibility to take corrective action for potential harm caused by agreeing to serve as U.S. counsel for foreign-domiciled trademark applications obtained via an intermediary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example corrective actions (as represented by Respondent) include mutually terminating the business relationship with the intermediary, contacting the intermediary to request transfer of matters, and, if no response, handling the matter on behalf of the client. Taking remedial steps is relevant to mitigation and ethical responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with investigation and expression of contrition (mitigating considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperation with OED's investigation and genuine contrition are noted as mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's full cooperation (candid responses, interviews) and expressed contrition were referenced as additional considerations in determining sanction. The Order notes these factors when describing the background and sanction decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and remedial requirements for violations (reprimand, probation, continuing legal education)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary sanctions can include reprimand, probation, mandatory continuing legal education, and other conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter Respondent agreed to: a reprimand; 12-month probation; within probation complete six (6) hours CLE (2 hours ethics/professional responsibility and 4 hours trademark law); and attestations of having reviewed TMEP, 37 C.F.R. §2.11, and relevant commentary. The Order explains sanctions as both punitive and corrective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and reporting obligations during probation (TESS searches and reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: During probation, practitioner must monitor USPTO records for filings naming them as attorney of record and report findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must: (i) on a weekly basis search the USPTO Trademark Electronic Search System (TESS) for applications identifying her as attorney of record and promptly inform appropriate USPTO persons of any filings not made by her or without her knowledge/consent; and (ii) on a quarterly basis submit a written report to the OED Director confirming completion of searches and stating whether any unauthorized listings were found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and procedures for alleged probation violations (Order to Show Cause; suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED Director believes respondent failed to comply during probation, OED will issue an Order to Show Cause and may seek suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED will issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to respondent's last address, and grant 15 days to respond. If OED still believes violations occurred after response, OED will deliver the Order, any response, and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension (up to 12 months) for the violations cited. Review of such action does not stay the suspension. OED may also seek discrete discipline for misconduct that formed the basis of the Order to Show Cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and use of disciplinary record
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders are publicly published and may be considered in future disciplinary actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director will electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's FOIA Reading Room and publish a materially consistent notice in the Official Gazette. The record of the disciplinary proceeding may be considered by the Office in addressing further complaints or future disciplinary proceedings (as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements).
